editorial.brief: Grand Theft Auto VI turned up on four feeds at once: 750,227 Wikipedia views, a 13,897,138-view YouTube video, a Lemmy post titled Grand task auto six and a match on Steam. Separately, Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia has the AI wire asking who comes next.
editorial.cover_sub: Grand Theft Auto VI drew 750,227 views, twice the runner-up, and also surfaced on Lemmy, Steam and YouTube, which makes it the one subject on which today's feeds agree.
editorial.wiki_deck: Grand Theft Auto VI led Wikipedia with 750,227 views, double the runner-up. It also appeared on three other feeds, a rare show of agreement from the internet.
editorial.letter_headline: A day with one game and one departure
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is anxious about a CVSS 9.8 OpenSSL overflow and Google versus GrapheneOS. Lemmy is angry about outages and subpoenas. Bluesky is gentle, with poetry and anniversaries. Mastodon is wry about tech billionaires.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire follows Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit and Anthropic IPO orders at six times supply, while the world searched for sri lanka vs pakistan, florida flash flooding and black friday.
editorial.markets_deck: The busiest market, at $1M, asks whether the Fed holds in December and gives 3% yes. Elsewhere: a 95% ceasefire, an 81% tennis match and a 1% Huang return.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,108,670 players on Steam, ahead of Dota 2 at 816,657 and PUBG at 729,448. On Twitch, caseoh_ holds 88,604 viewers, with TheBurntPeanut at 54,026 and xQc at 31,177.
editorial.yt_note: The GTA 6 challenge video leads on 13,897,138 views, well ahead of the Avengers: Doomsday trailer at 7,144,083. Two CMA Awards performances, Taylor Swift and Lainey Wilson, fill the list alongside a Nightingale teaser.
editorial.closing_note: Gone by tomorrow: the 705-point Grand task auto six post, the CMA Awards clips, and the Polymarket odds on Huang's return. Likely to remain: apple/FastFrames-L, still at 0 downloads, and the OpenSSL advisory, which needs patching whatever the news is doing.
wiki_paras: Grand Theft Auto VI was the most-read article on Wikipedia, with 750,227 views. Ramayana: Part 1 came second with 371,581, so the lead is 2.0 to one. The rest of the top five, Stephen Wilson Jr., Ella Langley and Ken McElroy, sit between 172,820 and 327,962.

The data offers no single cause, but it does offer company. The game appears on Lemmy, Steam and YouTube in the same snapshot. A YouTube video titled I Survived 100 Hours In GTA 6 has 13,897,138 views, and a Lemmy post titled Grand task auto six has a score of 705. Four feeds, one subject.

That makes it the day's cover story by default. The Lainey Wilson CMA Awards performance also crosses Wikipedia and YouTube, but at 446,359 views on YouTube it is a smaller affair. The data does not say what sent readers to GTA VI, only that they arrived on every feed together.
letter_paras: Today's snapshot is mostly single-story, with a side plot. Grand Theft Auto VI appears on four feeds, and the Nvidia chief executive's exit fills the AI wire. Nothing else crossed more than two feeds. The remaining pages are the ordinary run of security advisories, award-show performances and a Steam chart led by Counter-Strike 2.

In the unglamorous corners, Hugging Face lists apple/FastFrames-L at 0 downloads. Hacker News gave GIMP 66 points for acquiring UI tests, and the Polymarket odds on Jensen Huang rejoining Nvidia by November 30 stand at 1%. One Mastodon user reports lying on the floor to keep it company.

A snapshot taken in one minute removes the usual excuse. Every feed is read at the same moment, so a subject that shows up on four of them has earned the placement rather than drifted in over a week. The same-hour view also shows which stories are loud only in their own corner.
